# nimiq-branding-cli full reference

> The complete component registry of the nimiq-branding-cli in one flat markdown file: 64 Nimiq UI components (56 pixel-diffed against renders of the verbatim upstream source), each with purpose, props, dependencies, upstream source pins and the porting notes that carry the traps. Generated from registry/index.json and registry/components/*/meta.json by `nq sync-skill`.

Every component ships as a Vue 3 SFC and/or a plain HTML/CSS snippet. "Pixel-verified" means the HTML demo is rendered headlessly (Playwright, 2x scale, fonts settled, animations disabled) and diffed with pixelmatch against a render of the real upstream component; the diff must stay under the component's max diff threshold. The entries not pixel-verified (app-footer, app-header, connect-wallet-pill, corner-control, empty-state, flag-hex, provider-gate, status-pill) are original brand compositions with no upstream reference render. Each component's notes field is reproduced verbatim below: it records the sample state, harness traps and deliberate deviations from upstream, and is the highest-value part of this file. Machine-readable siblings: `registry/index.json` (index), `registry/components/<name>/meta.json` (per-component detail), `llms.txt` (discovery index).

## How to consume

Copy components with the CLI instead of re-implementing them; `nq add` brings the component plus its dependencies, CSS and real assets.

```
nq list                     # browse the registry (name, category, verified flag)
nq info <component>         # one component's purpose, props and CSS deps
nq init --style legacy      # drop Nimiq design tokens + base CSS into a project (or: modern)
nq add <component> --html   # copy a component into the project (or: --vue)
nq lint <file.html|url>     # enforce the brand rules on your own page
nq verify all               # (repo dev) re-run the pixel diffs against the references
```

## Nimiq Design Tokens — quick reference

Three token sets ship with this CLI. Pick ONE per project via `nq init --style modern|legacy|tokens-px`.

### Modern (`assets/css/modern/` — from onmax/nimiq-ui nimiq-css)

- 79 CSS custom properties in `colors.css`, all `oklch()` + `light-dark()` (automatic dark mode).
  Core hues: `--colors-neutral` (darkblue↔white), `--colors-blue`, `--colors-green`,
  `--colors-orange`, `--colors-red`, `--colors-gold`, `--colors-purple`, each with
  400/500/600/1100 tints. Brand navy: `--colors-darkblue: oklch(0.2737 0.068 276.29)` (#1F2348).
- Typography in `typography.css`, fonts in `fonts.css` (Mulish family).
- Layers: `preflight → colors → fonts → typography → spacing → utilities → atomic → animations`,
  linked together by `index.css`.

### Legacy (`assets/css/legacy/` — from @nimiq/style)

- `nimiq-style.min.css` — the `nq-*` class framework used by wallet.nimiq.com + hub:
  `nq-card`, `nq-card-header/body/footer`, `nq-button` (+ light-blue/green/orange/red variants),
  `nq-input`, `nq-label`, `nq-h1/h2`, `nq-text`, `nq-link`, `nq-icon`.
- Key hex values: Nimiq blue `#0582CA`, light blue `#265DD7`, gold `#E9B213`,
  navy text `#1F2348`, green `#21BCA5`, orange `#FC8702`, red `#D94432`.
  Radial gradients pair each color with a darker stop (e.g. blue `#265DD7→#0582CA`).
- Font: Muli/Mulish. Headings 600/700 weight. Base ease: `--nimiq-ease: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0, 0, 1)`.
- App card canon: `.small-page` = 420×564 px (52.5rem × 70.5rem at 8px root), radius 8px,
  shadow `0 3px 22px rgba(0,0,0,0.1)`. Pill CTAs 47px tall.

### Wallet app tokens (from `upstream/wallet/src`, 8px root)

Verified against the pinned wallet checkout (see `upstream-pins.json`).

- **Text opacity ladder** `--text-<step>`: the wallet's greyscale text system. Every step
  is Nimiq blue at descending alpha: `rgba(31, 35, 72, step/100)` via the `nimiq-blue()`
  helper (`scss/functions.scss`). Steps defined in `scss/themes.scss` (defaults mixin):
  `100, 80, 70, 60, 50, 40, 35, 30, 25, 22, 20, 16, 14, 12, 10, 6`.
  So `--text-70: rgba(31, 35, 72, 0.7)`, `--text-6: rgba(31, 35, 72, 0.06)`, etc.
  Prefer a ladder step over ad-hoc grays for any secondary text on light surfaces.
- **Crypto colors** (`scss/themes.scss` + asset classes, e.g. `BalanceDistribution.vue`):
  NIM `var(--nimiq-gold)` `#E9B213` (the gold brand color doubles as the NIM asset color),
  BTC `--bitcoin-orange: #F7931A`, USDC `--usdc-blue: #2775CA`,
  USDT `--usdt-green: #009393` (named green, renders teal).
- **Breakpoints (px)** (`scss/variables.scss`): mobile 768, tablet 960, halfMobile 1160,
  smallDesktop 1199, mediumDesktop 1319, largeDesktop 1409, extraLargeDesktop 1499,
  veryLargeDesktop 1800, ultraLargeDesktop 2000. Mirrored to JS via
  `scss/modules/variables.module.scss` + `variables.ts`.
- **App-shell layout widths (rem, 1rem = 8px)** (`App.vue` `#app` block):
  `--sidebar-width: 24rem` (192px), `--settings-width: 131rem`,
  `--address-column-width: 150rem`, `--account-column-width: 70rem` default (>= 1500px)
  stepping 65 / 59 / 52 / 47.5rem down the desktop breakpoints, 80.75rem >= 1800px,
  85rem >= 2000px, and 100vw (with address column) at <= 768px.

### tokens-px (`assets/css/tokens-px/` — the px-only escape hatch)

`nq init --style tokens-px` drops `nimiq/tokens-px/tokens.css`: every brand custom
property above (colors, the radial `-bg` gradients, radii, shadows, easing, font stacks,
the 16-step `--text-*` opacity ladder, crypto colors) as `:root` values in PLAIN PX /
absolute units — no `html{font-size}` rescale, no resets, no component classes. Use it
when hand-authoring CSS so you don't hit the legacy 8px-rem trap (and stop hand-copying
hex values per app). Tailwind v4 projects: import `tailwind-theme.css` (same values in an
`@theme` block) instead. Values sourced from the legacy sheet + wallet extraction above.

Full extraction with file paths: see `references/` in this repo and
`~/Projects/nimiq/nimiq-branding-skill/nimiq-branding.md` (deep brand doc).
@nimiq/utils API + live playground: `references/utils.md`, `references/utils-demo.html`.

## Component registry

64 components, 56 pixel-verified. Grouped by category (alphabetical), components alphabetical within each category.

### data-display

#### balance-distribution

Category: data-display. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 240x110, selector `.balance-distribution`).

Sidebar balance-distribution donut from the Nimiq wallet: a ring made of one rounded SVG arc per currency (gold NIM, orange BTC, blue USDC, teal USDT), sized by each currency's share of the account's total fiat value, next to a bold white CURRENCY / percentage legend. Empty currencies get no arc and a dimmed legend row; hovering a row or arc highlights that currency. Lives on the navy wallet sidebar.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| balances | Partial<Record<'nim' \| 'btc' \| 'usdc' \| 'usdt', number>> | no | { nim: 1, btc: 0 } | Fiat value per currency; each arc's length is the currency's share of the total. The keys decide which currencies appear (legend order: nim, btc, usdc, usdt; zero balances sort last). Upstream computes this from the Address/BtcAddress/PolygonAddress/Staking stores and Fiat exchange rates — the port exposes it as a prop. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: wallet@656ed56 (wallet:src/components/BalanceDistribution.vue)

Notes: Source: upstream/wallet/src/components/BalanceDistribution.vue (scoped styles verbatim) + layouts/Sidebar.vue for context (navy --bg-secondary: var(--nimiq-blue) background, 2.5rem vertical margin, Swap pill rendered below it by the sidebar — the pill is a sibling Tooltip/button, not part of this component). Sample state per brief item 6: NIM 100% / BTC 0% — BTC has no balance so only the gold NIM arc renders, as a full circle without gap or line caps (SVG_SIZE 51, STROKE_WIDTH 4, RADIUS 23.5, dasharray '147.655 0', dashoffset = circleStart = 32.914); the BTC legend row is .inactive (children at opacity .3). Currency colors: --nimiq-gold from the legacy framework; --bitcoin-orange #F7931A / --usdc-blue #2775CA / --usdt-green #009393 from wallet themes.scss, defined on the component root in the snippet. The upstream enter/leave arc transitions (transition-group hooks) are ported in the Vue variant; the html snippet is the static render.

#### copyable

Category: data-display. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 600x400, selector `.copyable`).

Wrapper that makes a click on its content copy it (or a provided text) to the clipboard, with a light-blue hover/focus tint and an animated 'Copied' tooltip as feedback.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| text | string | no | - | A specific text to copy to the clipboard on click. Defaults to the element's own innerText (minus the tooltip label). |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: vue-components@3c5b972 (vue-components:src/components/Copyable.vue)

Notes: Sample state: slot text 'NQ07 0000 ...' in resting (uncopied) state. The .background tint and .tooltip are opacity:0 at rest and only show on hover/focus/.copied. Tooltip label 'Copied' is the en-US i18n string. Clipboard.copy from @nimiq/utils is inlined verbatim in the Vue port (textarea + execCommand with selection restore). Upstream copies 800ms feedback (DISPLAY_TIME); keydown Space/Enter also triggers copy.

#### copyable-field

Category: data-display. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 560x260, selector `.nq-blue-bg`).

Labeled click-to-copy field for dark surfaces — an uppercase nq-label over a translucent white pill-radius field whose value copies on click with a 'Copied' notice; keyed values get small switcher buttons for alternative representations.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | string \| number \| { [key: string]: any } | yes | - | The value to display and copy. An object renders one .nq-button-s per key to switch between alternative representations (e.g. { hex: ..., base64: ... }); a string or number renders as a simple value with a right-edge fade mask. |
| label | string | no | - | Uppercase field label rendered above the value (nq-label at 50% white). |
| small | boolean | no | false | Compact variant: 5rem field height and 2.5rem default font size instead of 6.25rem and 3rem. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: vue-components@3c5b972 (vue-components:src/components/CopyableField.vue)

Notes: Sample state: label 'Address', simple string value 'NQ07 0000 0000 0000 0000', resting (uncopied), on a 60rem-wide navy .nq-blue-bg stage. The component renders WHITE text, so truth and demo sit on the navy surface and the verify selector crops .nq-blue-bg to capture the real look; .nq-blue-bg also swaps --nimiq-light-blue for the on-dark #0CA6FE that colors the 'Copied' notice. Upstream computes the value font size in JS (shrink-to-fit, default 3rem, 2.5rem when small); the sample value fits, so truth hardcodes font-size: 3rem inline and the demo's ported fit script computes the identical 3rem (min(3, 3 * scale)). Click copies the value (Clipboard.copy from @nimiq/utils, inlined verbatim in the Vue port) and shows the notice for 500ms; on simple values the .copied state also expands the right-edge fade mask (mask-size 160% to 100%). Keyed-value switcher buttons and the small variant carry full styles in the css but are not in the pixel sample. 'Copied' is the en-US i18n source string. Unlike Copyable, upstream CopyableField does not wrap the Copyable component, so there is no dependsOn. TRAP: the scoped .nq-label { color: rgba(255,255,255,.5) } only beats nimiq-style's .nq-blue-bg .nq-label { color: rgba(255,255,255,.7) } through Vue's scoped [data-v-*] attribute (specificity tie, later stylesheet wins); the truth reproduces the compiled scoping via [data-v-cf], and the namespaced .copyable-field .nq-label in the css variant resolves the tie the same way. Bare verbatim selectors render the label at the wrong alpha.

#### flag-hex

Category: data-display. Variants: vue, html. Verification: not pixel-verified (original brand composition, no upstream reference render).

A country flag clipped into the Nimiq rounded hexagon (the same shape as the identicon) — for language / country pickers. Handles the overscan, per-flag pan/zoom, aspect-correct fill (no letterbox), and one consistent gray edge so every flag reads cleanly including the pointed left/right tips.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| url | String | yes | - | Flag image URL. Vendor flags from `flag-icons` (MIT; flags are public domain). Use the 1x1 (square) file for most; the 4x3 file for wide/striped flags (see fit.aspect). |
| fit | { scale?: number; dx?: number; dy?: number; aspect?: number } | no | - | Pan/zoom the flag inside the hexagon. aspect = flag width/height (default 1 for 1x1 files, 4/3 for 4x3). scale zooms; dx/dy pan in SVG units (+x right, +y down). Keep scale >= (10 + max(\|dx\|,\|dy\|)) / 11 or the opposite edge uncovers (white gap). |

- source: original@null ()

Notes: ORIGINAL Nimiq-brand composition (not an upstream port), so `verified:false` — it reuses the VERBATIM Nimiq hexagon path (M19.964 8.156...). Hard-won rules baked in: (1) The hexagon is POINTED left/right — a naive clip crops vertical-stripe flags (France, Mexico) into slivers and leaves white at the tips; the image box overscans past the viewBox and overflow:visible lets the edge stroke reach the points. (2) preserveAspectRatio='slice' on a REFERENCED SVG <image> is letterboxed by browsers -> white line above/below; the fix is to size the image box to the flag's OWN aspect ratio (fit.aspect) so it covers with no letterbox. (3) flag-icons 1x1 (square) files STRETCH wide flags — e.g. the US canton becomes ~76% width; use the 4x3 source + fit.aspect=4/3 for the US. (4) Panning needs a matching zoom: scale >= (10+|pan|)/11 or the opposite edge uncovers. (5) Per-flag fit examples that took real tuning: US {aspect:4/3}, China {scale:1.2,dx:2.2,dy:2.8} (nudge the 5 stars into view), Korea {scale:0.84} (white margin around the taeguk/trigrams). (6) Every flag gets ONE faint gray edge rgba(31,35,72,0.22) stroke-width 0.4 so the shape + tips always read against a white page — uniform reads cleaner than per-flag colors. Flags are public-domain artwork; this snippet inlines simple tricolors (drawn as rects) so it is self-contained — swap the <g> for an <image href> pointing at your vendored flag file in real use. Pairs with the `identicon` component (same hexagon).

#### price-chart

Category: data-display. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 280x220, selector `.price-chart-widget`).

The wallet sidebar's crypto price sparkline — '24H' badge over a smoothed white line chart, with the currency ticker, fiat price and 24h percentage change below, on the navy sidebar background.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| currency | string | no | 'nim' | Crypto ticker shown bottom-left (rendered uppercase). Upstream: CryptoCurrency enum ('nim' \| 'btc' \| ...). |
| price | number | no | 0.000501 | Current fiat price. Formatted like @nimiq/vue-components FiatAmount with maxRelativeDeviation 0.001 (decimals grow until the rounded value is within 0.1%). |
| fiatCurrency | string | no | 'usd' | Fiat currency code for price formatting. |
| change | number | no | 0.001 | Relative price change over the time range (0.001 = +0.1%). Positive renders green with a CSS '+' prefix; upstream styles only .positive (negative stays 60% white). |
| points | { x: number, y: number }[] | no | 18-point sample NIM series | History points, normalized to the box by the upstream LineChart algorithm (cubic smoothing, factor 0.2). Upstream samples 18 points from the fiat history API. |
| showTimespanLabel | boolean | no | true | Show the '24H' pill (upstream: true for the first sidebar chart, false for the BTC one below it). Click emits 'timespan'. |
| timeRange | '24h' \| '7d' | no | '24h' | Label text for the timespan pill. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: wallet@656ed56 (wallet:src/components/PriceChart.vue, wallet:src/components/LineChart.vue)

Notes: Source: upstream/wallet/src/components/PriceChart.vue + LineChart.vue (scoped CSS verbatim, Vue scoping emulated with data-v attrs in truth), rendered in the wallet sidebar context: Sidebar.vue .price-chart-wrapper/.price-chart rules (height 15rem, padding 1.5rem, timespan moved to 1.5rem/1.5rem — Sidebar's ::v-deep override wins by injection order) on a 24rem-wide navy excerpt (--bg-secondary: var(--nimiq-blue), color white, --padding-sides 1.5rem from App.vue/Sidebar.vue). The .price-chart-widget root stands in for the sidebar; the wrapper's 3rem scroll-fade mask is omitted (it belongs to the full-height scrolling sidebar and would fade the meta row in this exact-height excerpt). Sample state: NIM, $0.000501, +0.1% (green), fixed deterministic 18-point 24h series; path precomputed with LineChart's exact calculatePath (smoothing 0.2, strokeWidth 2.5, viewBox padding 5) for the 144x52 svg box. White line is white at 0.5 stroke-opacity (currentColor), as upstream. Upstream pairs it with a second chart (currency='btc', showTimespanLabel=false) in the same wrapper. Wallet theme vars (--body-size, --small-size, --tiny-label-size) defined on the snippet root.

#### qr-code

Category: data-display. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 600x400, selector `canvas`).

Nimiq QR code — renders arbitrary data (typically a nimiq: payment URI) as a rounded-module QR code on a canvas, filled by default with the Nimiq light-blue radial gradient (#265DD7 → #0582CA) on a transparent background.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| data | String | yes | - | The data to encode. If falsy, the canvas is not rendered (v-if). |
| errorCorrection | String | no | M | Error correction level per QR spec: 'L' \| 'M' \| 'H' \| 'Q'. |
| radius | Number | no | 0.5 | Roundness of QR modules, 0–0.5. Recommended: 0.5. |
| fill | String \| LinearGradient \| RadialGradient | no | radial-gradient [1,1,0,1,1,√2] #265DD7 → #0582CA | Fill of the QR modules — hex color string or qr-creator gradient descriptor. Default is the Nimiq light-blue radial gradient (equivalent to nimiq-light-blue-bg). |
| background | String \| null | no | - | Background color (hex) or null for transparent. |
| size | Number | no | 240 | Width and height of the QR code in pixels (canvas pixels; the canvas has no devicePixelRatio scaling). |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- npmDeps: qr-creator
- source: vue-components@3c5b972 (vue-components:src/components/QrCode.vue)

Notes: Upstream QrCode.vue has no <style> block — the component is a bare <canvas class="qr-code">, all rendering done by qr-creator (pinned qr-creator@1.0.0, the only published version). Sample state: data 'nimiq:NQ07000000000000000000000000000000000000', size 240, all other props at upstream defaults. qr-creator sets canvas.width/height = size with no devicePixelRatio handling, so the QR renders at CSS-pixel resolution. The Vue port keeps the upstream toDataUrl() helper as an exposed method.

#### qr-scanner

Category: data-display. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 400x400, selector `.qr-scanner`).

Camera QR scanner — full-bleed video on the nimiq-blue gradient with a gold corner-frame viewport (pulsing while scanning), a white cancel pill and camera-failure guidance; scanning is powered by the qr-scanner library.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| reportFrequency | Number | no | 7000 | Minimum ms between repeated 'result' emits for the same scan result. |
| validate | Function | no | - | (scanResult: string) => boolean; results failing it are not emitted. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- npmDeps: qr-scanner
- source: vue-components@3c5b972 (vue-components:src/components/QrScanner.vue)

Notes: Sample state: the inactive/idle shell in a 300x300 box — the ONLY state a headless or permission-less context can show. The camera cannot run headless, so the pixel contract covers: video at opacity 0 (never .ready) over the nq-blue radial gradient, the corner-frame overlay with .inactive (white 40% stroke instead of gold, pulse animation off), the 'Your device does not have an accessible camera.' warning, and the white Cancel pill. JS-MEASURED GEOMETRY: repositionOverlay() sizes the overlay to ceil(2/3 * min(w,h)) = 200px and centers it (top/left 50px), written into element.style — the html variant freezes those numbers inline; recompute for other host sizes. SPECIFICITY TRAP: the scoped .cancel-button rules (background white, nimiq-blue text) tie with nimiq-style's .nq-button-s.inverse at (0,2,0) and win only through the scope attribute + source order — the truth keeps [data-v-scanner] on them; the html variant gets the same result from .qr-scanner .cancel-button. LIVE SCANNING (Vue variant only): wires the qr-scanner npm dep (QrScannerLib on the video element) — it needs a real camera, a user gesture in most browsers, and a secure context (HTTPS or localhost; getUserMedia is unavailable on plain HTTP). Camera access failures flip to the inactive state with per-browser unblock instructions (Chrome/Firefox/Safari, mobile vs desktop — BrowserDetection from @nimiq/utils is inlined) and retry every 3s. Emits 'result' (throttled by reportFrequency + validate), 'cancel', 'error'. The html variant is the static shell only.

#### tooltip

Category: data-display. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 500x400, selector `body`).

Hover/focus/click tooltip with a positioned arrow box. Wraps a trigger element (icon by default) and shows a dark Nimiq-blue gradient box with an arrow, positioned via a preferred '[primary] [secondary]' position (e.g. 'top right'), optionally constrained to a container.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| container | object ({ $el: HTMLElement }) | no | - | Container within which the tooltip should be positioned if possible. Constrains max-width and clamps placement. |
| disabled | boolean | no | false | Disables showing the tooltip. |
| noFocus | boolean | no | false | Removes the trigger from the tab order (tabindex -1). |
| preferredPosition | string | no | top right | Preferred position as '[primary] [secondary]' or '[primary]'. Primary is vertical (top/bottom) or horizontal (left/right); the optional secondary is of the opposite axis. Single primary centers on the other axis. |
| margin | Partial<Record<'top'\|'right'\|'bottom'\|'left', number>> | no | - | Margin to maintain to the container. Falls back to the container's padding per side. No effect without container. |
| autoWidth | boolean | no | false | Sets the tooltip's width to the container's width minus margin. No effect without container. |
| theme | 'normal' \| 'inverse' | no | normal | 'inverse' renders a white box with nimiq-blue text. |
| background | string | no | - | Background of the tooltip as a CSS value; overrides the theme (sets the --background CSS var, also used by the arrow). |
| styles | Partial<CSSStyleDeclaration> | no | - | Styles applied to the tooltip box (commonly width / minWidth) without deep CSS selectors. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: vue-components@3c5b972 (vue-components:src/components/Tooltip.vue)

Notes: Sample state: tooltip forced visible ('shown' class) with positionCssClass 'position-top-right' (the default preferredPosition 'top right' with no container), trigger = InfoCircleIcon from @nimiq/style, box text 'Transactions are free on Nimiq.', styles={ width: '25rem' } (real upstream usages always pass a width — without one the absolutely-positioned box shrink-wraps to near min-content). JS-computed inline position expanded by hand and measurement-verified: left = triggerWidth/2 - 25 = -16px, top = -boxHeight = -66px. Arrow = .trigger::after with an SVG mask-image; its background color for top-right is #211e45 (sampled from the nimiq-blue-bg radial gradient where the arrow touches the box). CSS vars --nimiq-blue/--nimiq-blue-bg/--nimiq-ease come from the legacy nimiq-style.min.css (defined on html{}). Vue 3 port keeps the full dynamic positioning/clamping logic, hover/focus/click behavior, show/hide events and container scroll listener; '>>>' deep selectors became :deep().

#### backup-codes

Category: feedback. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 520x340, selector `.card-stage`).

The Keyguard backup-codes illustration — two overlapping gradient chat bubbles labeled Nimiq Backup Code 1/2 and 2/2 (purple and red radial gradients with speech tails, white counter circles, redacted code lines) that walk the user through sending themselves their two backup codes.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|

- source: original@null ()

Notes: ORIGINAL composition (flag-hex precedent), so verified:false; reference.png is snapped from truth/truth.html and nq verify guards the demo against it as a regression check. There is no upstream empty-state component (the wallet's empty screen is a whole layout, not a reusable block), so this formalizes the fleet's de facto standard: chorecoin public/app.css .empty (padding 26px 18px, centered, muted, 14px 600, big emoji in the line), tipjar .tips-empty (28px 16px, 15px, 'plain body text on the white feed card, set by whitespace'), drip .empty (15px, dim, 3x space padding), nimpot and snappos .empty-note (14px, ink-50). V2 2026-07-10 after Andjroo's design review ('The block, that's ugly. The row inside a list has nothing. On navy, all caught up, that is terrible'): the raw-emoji default, the bare one-line row and the 'All caught up' sample copy are gone. Design decisions: (a) radical simplicity per PRINCIPLES law 4 still: whitespace + type hierarchy do the structural work; no borders, no boxes, no invented ornament; the component is transparent and the page or card supplies the surface. (b) Icon treatment: a real Nimiq duotone icon (assets/icons/duotone/*.svg) riding currentColor at the muted ink; the set's secondary shapes carry their own opacity .4 within the SAME color (skill icon rule: same color at .4, never a second hue). Sized by role per the skill: 80px in the block (the 80-130px spot/result illustration tier) and 20px beside the row line (the 16-24px glyph tier). Emoji stays possible via the slot (chorecoin legacy, 44px) but is no longer the demo or default; never a generic icon set. Demo icons chosen gradient-free (some duotone icons embed currentColor radialGradients whose duplicate ids could trip rule 3 when inlined twice): nim-phone (receive NIM on your wallet), cash-register (tips received), magnifying-glass (search/filter). (c) Type ladder calibrated against the wallet's real empty screen (screenshots/nimiq-wallet/wallet.nimiq.com-desktop.png: full-ink bold title over a muted secondary line, generous whitespace): .es-title 18px 700 full ink (#1F2348 / #FFF on dark), .es-message 15px 600 muted (navy 50% / white 60%; contrast ratios as before: navy .5 on white 3.11:1, deliberately matching the brand's own sub-AA secondary text which nq lint warns rather than gates; white .6 on flat navy 6.33:1, 6.93:1 on the gradient corner; action full-contrast navy on 7% tint 12.45:1, white on 20% inverse chip 7.95:1). Rhythm: 6px title-to-message via container gap, icon margin-bottom 14px (= 20px to title), action margin-top 18px (= 24px from message). (d) Row size is intentional, not bare: flex-row, 20px duotone glyph at the muted ink beside a single quiet 14px line, 10px gap, centered; still one line only, no title, no action. (e) The action is unchanged: the legacy .nq-button-s capsule converted from the 8px root to px (27px, padding 0 12px, 14px 700, neutral bg rgba(31,35,72,.07), hover .12 with darkened navy #151833, inverse white .2/.25 on dark), radius 999px on the skill's pill tier; focus-visible ring 2px #0582CA offset 3px; transitions ride --nimiq-ease with cubic-bezier(0.25, 0, 0, 1) fallback plus a prefers-reduced-motion guard. One primary action max (PRINCIPLES); navy, never green (rule 5). (f) Title and message are <p>, not headings, so empty states never pollute the page outline; copy stays short fragments with no periods (rule 16 discipline) and no dashes (rule 18); the 'All caught up' sample was dropped per Andjroo, demo copy is realistic fleet copy (No transactions yet / Receive your first NIM to get started + Receive NIM, No tips yet, No results for this filter + Clear filters). (g) Two sizes only: block for a page section and row for an empty list inside a card, the two scales the fleet actually ships. Demo (= truth) shows block on the #F8F8F8 page with the 80px nim-phone + title + secondary + action, row inside a white card (radius 10px, the app-card shadow 0 4px 28px rgba(0,0,0,.111)) with the cash-register glyph, and the on-dark block (magnifying-glass, white ink ladder, inverse action) on the navy radial (rule 7). Pairs with transaction-list and the card components; use status-alert for errors that need attention rather than an empty state. nq lint on demo.html: 0 errors; the two advisory warnings stay: the 27px tap target is the shipped legacy .nq-button-s height (3.375rem at the 8px root, same as v1), and the off-scale spacing values are the fleet's own row padding (26px, chorecoin) plus the v2 rhythm (10/14/18px, tuned to the wallet reference rather than snapped to the marketing scale).

#### provider-gate

Category: feedback. Variants: vue, html. Verification: not pixel-verified (original brand composition, no upstream reference render).

Suggested precedence: demo > simulated > open-in-wallet > testnet > connected. No hard app-shell dependency: any callback returning a state works. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- npmDeps: qr-creator
- source: original@null ()

Notes: ORIGINAL composition (flag-hex / app-header precedent), so verified:false; reference.png is still snapped from truth/truth.html and nq verify guards the demo against it as a regression check. There is no upstream provider banner: the Nimiq team builds the wallet and hub, not mini-app chrome, so this formalizes what 15 fleet apps hand-roll ('Demo mode' strips, 'Open inside Nimiq Pay' banners, testnet disclaimers, tipjar's handoff wall). Design decisions: (1) The strip extends the status-alert family, the ONE legitimate pill/callout family (rule 17): same nimiq-css token halves, same tint bg + 1.5px tonal outline (outline-offset -1.5px, uniform ring, NO left accent stripe per rule 19), same icon-mask mechanism, compacted to a one-line 14px/600 strip because it is page chrome, not a content callout. (2) States carry fixed, localizable copy so the fleet stops improvising wording; semantics follow the color rules: demo = neutral navy (a fact, not a warning; neutral-300/400 light halves from nimiq-css colors.css), open-in-wallet = blue info, connected = green success, testnet AND simulated = orange warning (coins with no value / fake settlement both warrant caution). (3) Icons are real assets, never fabricated (rule 15): demo = nimiq-icons icon:info, open-in-wallet = the status-alert note hexagon, connected = nimiq-icons icon:check, testnet/simulated = the status-alert warning flame; all via the status-alert mask mechanism colored by --pg-text. (4) The strip's optional action is a bold currentColor text link with hover underline (rule 21, the tipjar wall-link treatment), not a second button; negative-margin padding gives it and the wall's copy link a 36px tap target without growing the visual. (5) The wall is tipjar's public/onboard-core.js wallScreenHtml + app.css .wall-screen formalized: navy radial app card (rule 7, 10px app-card radius, the .nq-card shadow in px), verbatim hexagon signet (gradient id unique per instance, rule 3), 24px/700 white title with NO trailing period (rule 16, rendered as h2 so consuming pages keep one h1), white-60% message, QR on a white tile (the qr-code component recipe: pinned qr-creator@1.0.0, light-blue bottom-right radial fill), ONE primary action (.nq-button light-blue, never green per rule 5) and a quiet copy-link fallback in --nimiq-light-blue-on-dark #0CA6FE (rule 20). Copy-link copies the plain page URL (sendable anywhere), not the nimiqpay:// URI. (6) The driver (initProviderGate in html/provider-gate.js) is dependency-free: { state | detect, pageUrl?, deepLink?, wall?, labels? } -> { state, setState, refresh, destroy }; detect is the only integration seam and maps 1:1 to nimiq-app-shell src/wallet/detect.ts: detectModeSync() 'miniapp' -> connected, 'hub' -> open-in-wallet, tipjar probe.fake -> demo, mock settlement -> simulated, testnet network -> testnet (precedence: demo > simulated > open-in-wallet > testnet > connected). Only open-in-wallet blocks, and only when options.wall is set (tipjar shows the wall on desktop; on a phone the deep link button in the strip is enough). The wall QR renders only when qr-creator is loaded (window.QrCreator); without it the tile is omitted, nothing breaks. (7) nq lint: 0 errors, 1 accepted warning: white on #0582CA (4.16:1) is the shipped legacy .nq-button light-blue itself, which nimiq.com ships (the lint spec warns rather than gates sub-AA that the brand itself ships); the button uppercases itself (the class does it, rule 8); the strip is a status alert, the allowed pill family. No new colors, no shadows beyond the card shadow, no ornament; the one calculated break is the gold signet on the navy wall. Fleet refs: apps/tipjar public/onboard-core.js (the unit-tested 4-state wall this formalizes: install/get-started map onto open-in-wallet with the wall, demo maps to demo) + public/app.css .wall-screen, apps/splitlink public/index.html #banner + js/app.js (the strip: 'Demo mode... open inside Nimiq Pay' / 'Connected to Nimiq Pay'), nimiq-app-shell src/wallet/detect.ts (the detection seam). Heritage: status-alert (treatment), qr-code (QR recipe), app-header (unique gradient id + badge conventions; its orange Testnet badge pairs with this strip). Vue variant needs npm qr-creator; the html snippet loads the pinned CDN build.

#### status-alert

Status alert / callout block (note-info, tip-success, warning, caution-error, important) in the real Nimiq pattern: tinted background, 1.5px tonal outline, uppercase icon title and colored text. Used for status notices, warnings and error feedback.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| type | 'info' \| 'success' \| 'warning' \| 'error' \| 'important' | no | 'info' | Alert severity; maps to the upstream callout classes note/tip/warning/caution/important (blue/green/orange/red/purple). |
| title | string | no | '' | Title line text. Defaults to the upstream label for the type (Note/Tip/Warning/Caution/Important). Rendered uppercase with the type icon. |
| message | string | no | '' | Alert body text. The default slot overrides it when provided. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: nimiq-ui@68e96cd (nimiq-ui:packages/nimiq-vitepress-theme/src/assets/github-callouts.css)

Notes: REBUILT 2026-06-11: previous port came from a local example file (icon-chip + navy text + 1px border) which is NOT a real Nimiq pattern. Source of truth now = upstream/nimiq-ui/packages/nimiq-vitepress-theme/src/assets/github-callouts.css (.custom-block.github-alert), the alert pattern nimiq-branding-skill/references/status-alerts.md cites; color tokens inlined as the light-mode halves of light-dark() from upstream/nimiq-ui/packages/nimiq-css/src/css/colors.css. Truth keeps the component CSS verbatim and restores the upstream docs context (html/body 16px; @nimiq/style's 8px rem base would halve the rem padding). Snippet/Vue porting decisions: rem converted to px at the upstream 16px root (padding 1rem 1.25rem -> 16px 20px) and font-size:16px pinned on the root class so the snippet renders identically under @nimiq/style; selectors renamed/namespaced under .nq-status-alert; the upstream docs full-bleed quirk (transform translateX(-8px) + width calc(100%+16px)) is kept for pixel parity — consumers can delete that pair for a non-bleeding alert. The legacy framework's own inline pattern is .nq-notice (colored text only), already covered by upstream apps; this component is the block-level alert. No upstream Vue component exists (callouts are markdown-rendered), so the Vue port is a faithful wrapper (type/title/message props + slot).

#### status-pill

Category: feedback. Variants: vue, html. Verification: not pixel-verified (original brand composition, no upstream reference render).

The fleet's semantic status chip, the ONE legitimate pill (rule 17): success/warning/error/info/neutral families plus testnet/mainnet/demo/live/simulated environment presets, as a 10% semantic tint with an AA ink on light and semantic ink on the wallet's white .07 chip on dark. Replaces the badge/tag/pill 12 apps hand-roll.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| type | String | no | 'neutral' | Semantic family (success \| warning \| error \| info \| neutral) or environment preset (testnet/simulated -> warning, mainnet/live -> success, demo -> neutral). Unknown values fall back to neutral. HTML variant: the same words as classes on .status-pill; preset classes ship as CSS aliases. |
| dark | Boolean | no | false | On-dark variant for navy surfaces: white .07 chip + on-dark inks (the wallet testnet treatment). HTML variant: add class 'on-dark'. |
| label | String | no | undefined | Pill text; defaults to the type word. The default slot overrides both. CSS uppercases it. Keep it a status word, never a decorative label. |

- source: original@null ()

Notes: ORIGINAL composition (flag-hex precedent), so verified:false; reference.png is snapped from truth/truth.html and nq verify guards the demo against it as a regression check. PARTIAL upstream heritage rather than a single portable source: (1) the legacy .nq-button-s colored recipe in nimiq-style.min.css is the tint formula (semantic color at 10% alpha + full-strength ink, e.g. rgba(33,188,165,.1); neutral rgba(31,35,72,.07)); (2) the wallet Sidebar.vue .testnet-notice is the on-dark treatment (orange label on rgba(255,255,255,.07)), the same treatment app-header ships as its badge; (3) swellet brand.ts pill() contributes the one-class-per-MEANING family mapping (its 12% tint was normalized to the upstream 10%, which snappos .sim-banner also uses). Fleet refs replaced: bounti .badge, splitlink .mode-badge, nimpot .net-pill, chorecoin .tag, snappos .sim-tag. METRICS are the app-header badge verbatim (Mulish 700, 12px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.09em, line-height 1, padding 5px 8px, radius 4px) so the badge slot can host a status-pill seamlessly; Mulish 700 over Fira Mono because every fleet pill ships bold Mulish and Fira Mono is reserved for technical values (addresses, keys, numbers), not UI labels; radius 4px is the skill's chip tier (chips 3 to 4px) and the app-header badge value, chosen over the fleet's occasional 999px full round for the same slot-compatibility reason. CONTRAST, all combinations computed (WCAG 2.x, alpha composited): on light, tint over a white card / over the #F8F8F8 page: success #3A766F 4.81/4.55, warning #985F1D 4.81/4.55, error #B53121 5.35/5.06, info #265DD7 5.10/4.82, neutral rgba(31,35,72,.7) 5.34/5.18; on dark, ink on the white .07 chip over flat #1F2348 (worst case) / over the gradient corner #260133: success #21BCA5 5.14/6.66, warning #FC8702 5.02/6.51, error #FF735D 4.59/5.95, info #0CA6FE 4.61/5.98, neutral rgba(255,255,255,.7) 6.89/8.32. Every combination clears 4.5:1. INK DERIVATIONS: full-strength palette tokens fail AA on their own light tints (green 2.2, orange 2.6), so each on-light ink is the darkest same-hue shade inside the palette envelope (nq lint rule 13 gates any color further than delta 55 from a brand anchor): error is #B53121, the nimiq-css --colors-red-1100 light half (oklch 0.515 0.1713 30.54) converted to sRGB, delta 44; info is #265DD7, the shipped light-blue gradient start, delta 0; success #3A766F holds the brand green's own hue 173 at delta 55 from the green gradient start #41A38E (the nimiq-css --colors-green-1100 light half lands at delta 64 and would fail lint); warning #985F1D is the darkest amber on the orange hue side (hue 32, delta 54; no orange-family ink can pass 4.5:1 on a light tint closer than that because the darkest lint-legal pure orange tops out at 3.3). On dark the base tokens green/orange already pass on the chip so no swap is needed (which is why legacy defines none); blue swaps to --nimiq-light-blue-on-dark #0CA6FE per rule 20; red needs more than the shipped --nimiq-red-on-dark #FF5C48 (4.01 on the chip), so #FF735D raises it along its own oklch hue line (0.2018 chroma, hue 30) to L 0.755. DESIGN GUARDS: no colored-dot chips (banned ornament; drip's dot deliberately not ported), no icons, no gradient on the chip (the tint is not a saturated color area and its .nq-button-s ancestor is also flat), non-interactive so no hover states, sentence-case source text uppercased by CSS. nq lint reports colored-uppercase warnings for the pills; accepted deliberately with the wallet testnet-notice citation (the app-header badge precedent). The demo (= truth) shows all ten states on both surfaces: light pills inside a white card, their canonical fleet host; dark pills directly on the navy radial (rule 7). Pairs with app-header (badge slot) and status-alert (block-level alerts; this is the inline chip).

Element is 3.25rem = 26px square (1rem = 8px). Geometry derived in JS upstream: fullCircleLength=2*PI*r; time arc capped below a full circle (gap >= 2.5 strokeWidths) so it always reads as a timer; filler arc fills the gap minus strokeWidth margins; both offset by 90deg so the gap is centered on top. Notes: Source of truth: upstream/wallet/src/components/swap/SwapNotification.vue (the wallet's bottom toast), SCSS hand-compiled with $mobileBreakpoint=768px from wallet/src/scss/variables.scss; wallet globals button.reset/.flex-row/.flex-column/--body-size/--small-label-size from wallet/src/scss/themes.scss; icons from @nimiq/style (checkmark.svg, alert-triangle.svg, stopwatch.svg) via vue-components IconBase (adds class nq-icon), spinner from vue-components LoadingSpinner.vue, maximize glyph from wallet icons/MaximizeIcon.vue. BottomOverlay.vue (vue-components, used by UpdateNotification.vue) was the other candidate but has no error/success-vs-info color system, so SwapNotification was chosen as the canonical toast. Sample state: three toasts — info/in-progress (blue), error (orange) and success (green) — sitting IN the page flow on a compact .toast-stage (flex column, 12px gap, 24px padding; page chrome overrides position:fixed to position:relative at stage level so the absolute maximize glyph keeps its anchor). Restaged 2026-07-10 (Andjroo feedback: the old demo rendered three fixed-position toasts floating over a huge empty canvas): the stage is page chrome only, component CSS unchanged, and reference.png now captures .toast-stage tightly (verify selector .toast-stage, 360x320 viewport) instead of the whole 800x320 body. Upstream quirks preserved: toast is position:fixed and is a <button class="reset"> that re-opens the swap modal; success state has no maximize glyph and pads the checkmark by 0.5rem; spinner keyframes get cancelled by the screenshot harness (animations:disabled) so renders are deterministic. Vue port is a faithful Vue 3 script-setup wrapper written for this registry (type/title/message props pick gradient + built-in icon). DRIVER (html/toast.js, ships with `nq add toast-notification`): zero-dep singleton `toast(message, {kind = 'info'|'success'|'error', duration = 2600})` — builds one bottom-center host (role=status, aria-live=polite) from this component's exact markup/classes, replace-not-queue, auto-dismiss (duration <= 0 = sticky), click dismisses, prefers-reduced-motion drops the slide/fade, returns {el, dismiss}. 'warning' also accepted (the fourth verified state); unknown kinds fall back to info. Attaches as window.nqToast (+ window.toast when free); works as classic script or ESM side-effect import. Requires this component's CSS on the page; the driver injects only its own host-placement/motion CSS and never touches component styles. Live demo: visible by default in html/demo.html (Andjroo 2026-07-10: 'Toast driver, I see nothing' — the old ?live gating hid it): a Try-the-driver row (Show info/success/error toast, neutral .nq-button-s so no rule-5 color wobble) wired to window.nqToast; driver toasts appear fixed bottom-center, clear of the static stage, and the pixel contract is unaffected because reference.png captures .toast-stage only. nq lint on demo.html: 0 errors; remaining warnings are upstream-verbatim or advisory and stay: white .7 sub-line on the orange gradient is the wallet's own toast text (sub-AA like nimiq.com's secondary grey, warn-not-gate), the 27px tap target is the shipped .nq-button-s height (3.375rem at the 8px root), and the 20px off-scale spacing comes from the legacy .nq-h2/.nq-text margins.

#### close-button

#### connect-wallet-pill

Category: form. Variants: vue, html. Verification: not pixel-verified (original brand composition, no upstream reference render).

The fleet's wallet connect button: one pill that walks connect -> busy (spinner) -> connected chip (identicon + truncated address + optional NIM balance), with a tap-twice disconnect. A small vanilla driver (initConnectPill) takes a pluggable async connect callback, designed for the nimiq-app-shell createWallet seam. Replaces 6 divergent bespoke connect buttons.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| connect | async () => ({ address, label?, balance? } \| null) | yes | - | The only integration point. Sit it on nimiq-app-shell: connect: () => wallet.connect(). Resolve null on cancel (or when a mobile redirect is in flight) and the pill returns to idle. No hard dependency on the app-shell: any async callback works. |
| onDisconnect | () => void | no | - | Called after the user confirms disconnect on the chip (e.g. wallet.disconnect()). |
| account | { address, label?, balance? } | no | - | Initial account: restores a persisted session straight into the connected chip. |
| labels | { connect?, connecting?, disconnect? } | no | { connect: 'Connect wallet', connecting: 'Connecting', disconnect: 'Disconnect' } | Localizable labels. |
| identicon | async (address) => url | no | - | Identicon resolver. Default: window.Iqons.toDataUrl when @nimiq/iqons is loaded (pinned 1.6.0, house recipe), else the hexagon placeholder. |
| formatBalance | (balance) => string | no | - | Balance formatter. Default: thin-space grouped NIM ('1 234 NIM'); strings pass through. |
| onError | (err) => void | no | - | Called when the connect callback rejects (the pill returns to idle). Default: console.error. |
| class: on-dark | css class on the button | no | - | On navy surfaces (e.g. inside app-header): flat white-alpha pill (the shipped .nq-button-s.inverse alphas) instead of the navy radial. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- npmDeps: @nimiq/iqons
- assetFiles: img/iqons.min.svg
- source: original@null ()

Notes: ORIGINAL composition (flag-hex precedent), so verified:false; reference.png is still snapped from truth/truth.html and nq verify guards the demo against it as a regression check. There is no upstream connect button: the wallet/hub own the other side of the popup, so this formalizes the best fleet pattern (hashmark renderTopbarAddress, a 3-state topbar chip whose CSS was off-brand) on shipped nq tokens. RESTAGED 2026-07-11 on Andjroo's direct feedback: 'the cards they're on right now look terrible, dark on dark. On the connected state it would have the identicon next to it.' The pill CSS and its tokens are UNCHANGED; what changed is the demo/truth staging: (a) the old bare navy panel is gone; the three states sit on a white card on the light stage, (b) the pill is then shown mounted inside its REAL host context, the redesigned app-header bars from this registry (light bar: custom nimiq.school brand + language selector + connected chip; navy bar: brand + testnet badge + language selector + connected on-dark chip), (c) every connected chip renders the identicon, PRE-RENDERED to a static data-url from the vendored team sprite (assets/img/iqons.min.svg + the pinned @nimiq/iqons@1.6.0 library, Iqons.toDataUrl over http against the local sprite) so the snapped reference is deterministic: no CDN race, no placeholder visible. Re-run that recipe if the demo address changes; the demo's live playground still does the runtime local-sprite-first dance. Judged against the snap, the on-dark connected chip on the shipped white .2 inverse surface reads clearly inside the navy bar (identicon + white ink, no navy-on-navy), so NO token step-up was taken; the inverse ladder (.2 rest, .25 hover, tokens.md) stays as shipped. nq lint on the restaged demo: 0 errors; its two warnings (the colored-uppercase Testnet badge, the 10px/20px flagship spacing) come from the embedded host header and are justified in app-header's notes. Design decisions: (1) Every surface is a shipped token, nothing invented: idle = the navy radial pill (nq-button-pill treatment, bottom-right anchor, darkened-gradient hover via the nq-button ::before pattern); connected/confirm = the quiet .nq-button-s surface (navy .07 rest, .12 hover) because a connected chip is status, not a call to action; on-dark = the shipped .nq-button-s.inverse alphas (white .2 rest, .25 hover; flat fills are canonical for white/secondary pills; white .2 rather than a bespoke lower alpha because it is the real shipped inverse token). (2) Type is the nq-button-s scale (14px/700 Mulish) written in px so the 8px-root rem trap cannot bite; height is 32px, raised from the legacy 27px to clear nq lint's 30px mobile tap floor. (3) The spinner is the CircleSpinner arc geometry (upstream vue-components) recolored via currentColor per the icon rule, with prefers-reduced-motion handling; busy keeps the surface (no disabled-gray flash for a sub-second popup roundtrip). (4) The address is a technical value: Fira Mono, uppercase, truncated to the first 7 + last 5 characters of the space-formatted address around an ellipsis (NQ87 JY...CVN2); the full formatted address rides in title. Optional balance sits one opacity step down (60%, wallet text ladder) with thin-space grouping. (5) Disconnect stays radically simple: tap the chip and it flips to a Disconnect label (confirm state, same quiet surface since red = error only and disconnecting is not an error), tap again to disconnect; outside click, Escape, or 4s reverts. One element, no menu. (6) Identicon via the house iqons recipe (pinned @nimiq/iqons@1.6.0 on jsdelivr, vendored team-shipped iqons.min.svg sprite with byte-identical CDN fallback, see swap-balance-bar); the driver falls back to the hexagon placeholder when iqons is absent, and races nothing: the chip renders immediately on the placeholder and swaps in the iqon (guarded against stale renders). (7) Keyboard focus = the house 2px blue ring outside the pill (:focus-visible; 0CA6FE on dark per rule 20). The one calculated break is the identicon itself. Driver returns { state, account, setAccount, setBalance, disconnect, destroy }; setAccount wires wallet.onAccountChange (the hashmark mobile-redirect return path). Fleet refs: hashmark-test-pool app/src/client/main.ts renderTopbarAddress, nimiq-app-shell src/wallet (createWallet/Account), tipjar identicon placeholder. Pairs with app-header (mount in its tools slot with class on-dark).

#### language-selector

Category: form. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 240x340, selector `.language-selector`).

Locale dropdown — an uppercase trigger with a small caret that opens a navy gradient list of locale codes on focus, with keyboard navigation; used to switch the UI language.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| languages | string[] | yes | - | Locale codes to offer (e.g. ['en', 'de', 'es', 'fr']). Must be a non-empty array of strings; a single entry renders the trigger without arrow or list. |
| value | string | no | - | The selected locale, compatible with Vue 2 v-model (pairs with the 'input' emit). Defaults to the first entry of languages; values not in the list are ignored. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: vue-components@3c5b972 (vue-components:src/components/LanguageSelector.vue)

Notes: Sample state: closed, languages [en, de, es, fr, nl, pt], selected 'en' (renders EN via text-transform uppercase). Closed means the .list element is NOT in the DOM (upstream v-if) — the trigger arrow's closed orientation is driven by the :not(:where(:hover, :focus-within, :has(.list))) rule, so the HTML snippet also creates/removes the list dynamically instead of toggling visibility. Open state: navy .list (--nimiq-blue-bg bottom-right radial) overlays the trigger from bottom:-2rem, entries at opacity .4 that go full plus a white arrow on focus; the list opens on focus (focusin), closes on blur with upstream's 50ms delay so focus can move between entries, arrow keys wrap, Enter/Space select, Escape/Left close. The tabindex is removed while open, like upstream's :tabindex binding. The snippet fires an 'input' CustomEvent (detail = locale code) as the plain-HTML equivalent of the Vue emit. Not carried into the snippet: the .transition-fade opacity animation on open/close (entries appear without fade; noted, cosmetic only). #### long-press-button

Category: form. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 420x180, selector `.long-press-button`).

Hold-to-confirm button — a nq-button whose white progress pill fills over the hold duration, swapping the label to 'Keep pressing…' at 40% and firing 'long-press' at 100%; protects critical actions from accidental clicks.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| duration | number | no | 3000 | How long the button must be held before 'long-press' fires, in milliseconds. Also drives the fill speed and the 40% 'Keep pressing…' prompt delay. |
| color | string | no | light-blue | A nimiq-style button color class (light-blue, green, orange, red, gold) or 'inverse' for colored backgrounds (requires the button to share the background's stacking context). |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: vue-components@3c5b972 (vue-components:src/components/LongPressButton.vue)

Notes: Sample state: rest (not pressed, no .indicator in the DOM), color light-blue (upstream default), slot label 'Hold to confirm', no subline; the frozen frame is exactly this rest state. Requires the nq-button base from nimiq-style.min.css (class='long-press-button nq-button light-blue'). Pressed behavior (interactive in the snippet/demo, not in the frozen frame): mousedown/touchstart/Enter/Space inserts the .indicator at width 0 which transitions to full width over duration ms; at duration*0.4 the labels cross-fade to 'Keep pressing…' (the ellipsis is the upstream \u2026 i18n string); at duration a 'long-press' CustomEvent fires; releasing early (document mouseup, touchend, keyup, blur) rewinds the fill within min(.3s, duration). Click events are swallowed (preventDefault + stopImmediatePropagation), only 'long-press' confirms. Both labels always stay in the DOM so the button never resizes. The label color switch inside the fill is two nested mix-blend-modes (mask lighten, indicator difference), which is why labels transition color/margin instead of opacity/transform (a new stacking context would break the blend). Vue 3 port trap: upstream's Vue 2 '.transition-indicator-enter' class is renamed '-enter-from'.

#### password-box

Category: form. Variants: vue, html. Verification: pixel-verified, max diff 0.5% (viewport 500x560, selector `.password-box-demo`).

The Keyguard PIN/password unlock box — a light-blue gradient action box with centered masked dots, a show/hide eye toggle, the prompt label and a white pill Unlock button, plus the hexagon loading state shown while the key is being decrypted.

| Prop | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| value | string | no | '' | The password text, bindable via v-model (emits 'input'). Sample/demo: 8 characters -> input-eligible. |
| masked | boolean | no | true | Masks the input as dots (input type password). The eye button toggles it via update:masked; visible text drops the wide letter-spacing, as upstream. |
| loading | boolean | no | false | Shows the hexagon spinner centered in the box and hides everything else, replacing upstream's global body.loading + .page:target gate. Spinner freezes at its stylesheet dash offsets when animations are disabled and under prefers-reduced-motion. |
| prompt | string | no | 'Enter your password' | Prompt label. Upstream shows 'Enter your PIN' when minLength equals Key.PIN_LENGTH (6). |
| buttonLabel | string | no | 'Unlock' | Submit button text, standing in for upstream's buttonI18nTag variants (Unlock, Confirm transaction, Show recovery words, ...). |
| minLength | number | no | 8 | Characters required before the box becomes input-eligible (input rises, button fades in). PasswordInput.DEFAULT_MIN_LENGTH = 8; PIN = 6. |
| bgColor | string | no | 'light-blue' | Upstream bgColor option: the box gets nq-<bgColor>-bg and the button gets that color class (inverse while the input is shown). |
| hideInput | boolean | no | false | No password required (unencrypted key): hides prompt and input, shows only the button on the plain card. |

- cssFiles: css/legacy/nimiq-style.min.css
- source: keyguard@02e7534 (keyguard:src/components/PasswordBox.js, keyguard:src/components/PasswordBox.css, keyguard:src/components/PasswordInput.js, keyguard:src/components/PasswordInput.css, keyguard:src/common.css)

Notes: Source: upstream/keyguard src/components/PasswordBox.js/.css (markup with default bgColor 'light-blue' and the 'passwordbox-log-in' button 'Unlock' as used by ExportBackupCodes.js) + src/components/PasswordInput.js/.css (input-container/input-wrapper/eye-button) + src/common.css (.actionbox and the password-box loading-spinner positioning + hexagon keyframes). Sample state: two stacked boxes at 51rem (the .page-footer width of the 52.5rem Keyguard card): (1) 8 characters entered -> input-eligible with masked dots, eye toggle and the raised white Unlock pill; (2) the same box with the loading gate active, only the hexagon spinner visible. Icons are verbatim team assets, never redrawn: the eye toggle is @nimiq/style nimiq-style.icons.svg #nq-view-off/#nq-view inlined as the .is-visible/.not-visible groups (the upstream <use> pair, resolved for file:// rendering, same approach as close-button), and the hexagon spinner is the inline SVG from PasswordBox.js byte-identical (same paths as the loading-spinner component). Deviations, all documented: upstream's loading gate is global (body.loading .page:target ...) and cannot show loading and non-loading boxes on one page, so both truth and port scope those exact declarations to a .loading class on the box; hexagon keyframes are prefixed password-box-* in the port (truth keeps upstream's loading-big-hex/loading-small-hex names); common.css .actionbox is folded into a single-class .password-box selector so the later padding override wins by order like upstream's file order (a .password-box.actionbox selector would out-specify it); the port adds a prefers-reduced-motion guard. When animations are disabled the spinner renders at stroke-dashoffset -40.5/13 (identical to the 0% keyframes) — deterministic. The nq-light-blue-bg gradient, nq-input, nq-button light-blue inverse and --nimiq-ease all come from the vendored nimiq-style.min.css. Vue port maps upstream options to props (value/masked/loading/prompt/buttonLabel/minLength/bgColor/hideInput), emits input/update:masked/submit and exposes focus(); the shake-on-wrong-password animation is not ported.
